findings.description: The old code fetched all keys with one catalog.get_many(locale, wanted). The new loop calls catalog.exists and then catalog.get for every key in every locale of the chain. That is up to 2 * keys * chain-length calls. If the catalog is backed by a DB or file, this becomes an N+1 pattern, and the two calls per key are also not atomic.
findings.suggestion: Use catalog.get_many per locale in the chain, only for the keys still unresolved, so the number of calls is bounded by the chain length.
findings.title: Per-key catalog lookups replace the batched get_many call

findings.description: Bundle.locale is set to chain[0], the normalised tag (for example pt_br becomes pt-BR), not the locale the caller passed in. Callers and missing_report that key on the requested locale string now get a different value. A catalog that stores non-canonical names, such as pt_BR, will also never match the normalised candidates, so every key is reported missing.
findings.suggestion: Keep the caller's requested locale in Bundle.locale, or ensure the catalog is queried with matching keys. Compare sources against the normalised chain[0] consistently.
findings.title: Bundle locale is normalised, which breaks the fallback_keys comparison and callers
